title: Drink And Trade Empties
statement:
You start with full full bottles of juice. Drinking a bottle leaves an empty one. At any time a shop swaps trade empty bottles for one new full bottle, as often as you can pay.

Return the largest total number of bottles you can drink.

examples.why: Drink 10, trade 8 empties for 2 (2 empties left over). Drink 2: now 4 empties, trade for 1 more. Drink it: 10 + 2 + 1.
5, then 2 (one empty kept), then the leftover joins the 2 new empties: 1, then 1. Dropping leftovers would give only 8.
Six empties are not enough for a single trade.

hints: Track two numbers: full bottles in hand and empties in hand. What happens in one round?
One round: drink every full bottle, then trade as many empties as you can. Remember to keep the remainder of the trade.
Each trade really costs trade − 1 empties, because the new bottle becomes an empty again. That gives a closed formula.

explain.intuition:
Simulate rounds. Drink everything you hold; the empties pile up. Trade ⌊empties / trade⌋ batches for new bottles and keep empties mod trade for later. Stop when you hold no full bottle.

There is also a shortcut. After drinking, each trade takes trade empties and the bottle you get back turns into one empty, so the net cost is trade − 1. You can keep trading while you hold at least trade empties, which gives full + ⌊(full − 1) / (trade − 1)⌋.
steps: While empty ≥ trade: got = ⌊empty / trade⌋, drunk += got, empty = empty mod trade + got.
pitfalls: Throwing away the leftover empties after a trade. In the second example that loses one bottle.
Forgetting that freshly drunk bottles become empties that can be traded again.
Using full / (trade − 1) in the formula instead of (full − 1) / (trade − 1): you can never trade your very last empty.

complexity.time: O(log full) for the loop, O(1) for the formula

solutions.title: Simulate rounds
solutions.idea: Drink, trade full batches of empties, keep the remainder, repeat.

solutions.title: Closed formula
solutions.idea: Each trade nets a cost of trade − 1 empties, and the last empty can never be spent.

followups: The shop now raises its price by one empty after every trade. How does the loop change?
You may borrow one empty from the shop and return it at the end. Does the formula change?
